FieldShift – Agricultural Digital Twin & Crop Rotation Simulator
Challenge: Field Shift – Adapting Farms with NASA Data | Pilot Region: Chaouia–Settat, Morocco

FieldShift is an interactive agricultural decision-support platform that helps farmers explore climate-resilient crop rotation strategies using NASA Earth observation data. Facing irregular rainfall, rising temperatures, and water scarcity in semi-arid regions like Chaouia–Settat, growers need practical tools to turn environmental data into clear seasonal choices.

Built with Python, Streamlit, Plotly, and the NASA POWER agro-climatology API, FieldShift translates historical temperature, precipitation, and solar radiation records into an accessible Agricultural Digital Twin through five core modules:

* Earth Memory: Visualizes multi-year climate history to separate long-term shifts from single-season weather.


* Soil Debt: Quantifies cumulative environmental and water pressure through an experimental screening index.


* What If? Lab: Compares baseline rotations against legume- and cover-crop alternatives weighted by farmer priorities (Water, Soil, or Balanced).


* Farm Time Machine: Connects past baselines, recent climate signals, and conditional future scenarios.


* Why Not?: Explains scoring assumptions, uncertainties, and local agronomic limits.



Our Vision: Every field has a memory. Every decision shapes its future.

FieldShift – Agricultural Digital Twin & Crop Rotation Simulator

Challenge: Field Shift – Adapting Farms with NASA Data

Pilot Region: Chaouia–Settat, Morocco

What It Does & How It Works

FieldShift is an interactive agricultural decision-support platform built around the concept of a farmer-centered Agricultural Digital Twin. Focused initially on the Chaouia–Settat agricultural plain in Morocco (including hubs such as Settat and Berrechid), it transforms multi-year NASA Earth observation data into clear, visual insights that help farmers evaluate environmental pressures and test climate-resilient crop rotation scenarios before making seasonal planting decisions.

Users configure their specific farm profile—selecting geographic location, land size (in hectares), soil texture (Clay, Loam, Sandy, or Unknown), water access regime (Rainfed, Limited, or Available irrigation), and management priority (Water conservation, Soil support, or Balanced). FieldShift then connects directly to the NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) agro-climatology API to retrieve historical monthly time series for 2-meter air temperature (T2M), corrected precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), and surface shortwave solar radiation (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN), with a seamless fallback to clearly labeled illustrative data when offline.

The platform guides farmers through five interconnected modules:

  1. Earth Memory: Reconstructs 5 to 20 years of local climate history using interactive charts and summary metrics (mean temperature, annual rainfall, first-to-last-year rainfall delta, and extreme heat months >30 °C) to distinguish long-term climate shifts from single-season weather fluctuations.
  2. Soil Debt: Calculates a transparent, experimental Environmental Pressure Index (0–100) combining rainfall deficit proxies, recent heat stress, and bare-soil exposure indicators to highlight cumulative ecological strain on farmland.
  3. What If? Lab: Lets farmers compare their baseline crop rotation (e.g., continuous wheat monoculture) against diversified 3-season rotations incorporating drought-tolerant cereals, nitrogen-fixing legumes (chickpea, lentil, faba bean), and cover crop mixes. Each sequence is scored across Water, Soil-Support, and Climate-Fit dimensions weighted by the farmer’s chosen priority.
  4. Farm Time Machine: Organizes insights across Past (early vs. recent multi-year rainfall comparisons), Present (latest monthly climate signals), and Future (conditional scenario simulations).
  5. Why Not?: Documents all scoring formulas, priority weights, assumptions, and scientific limitations alongside a practical pre-action checklist.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Making NASA Data Actionable: Translates raw gridded agro-climatological parameters into intuitive visual diagnostics tailored to local farm parameters rather than technical scientific tables.
  • Supporting Climate Resilience & Water Conservation: Helps semi-arid and rainfed farms evaluate trade-offs between water-intensive cereals and restorative legumes or cover crops, encouraging sustainable soil stewardship and reduced vulnerability to erratic rainfall.
  • Human-Centered & Ethical Decision Support: Prevents over-reliance on uncalibrated models by explicitly separating illustrative data from NASA observations and reminding users that satellite pixels complement—rather than replace—agronomists and laboratory soil tests.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Programming Language: Python 3.10+
  • Web Framework & UI: Streamlit (with custom CSS for a clean, accessible, high-contrast interface)
  • Data Processing & Numerical Analysis: Pandas and NumPy
  • Interactive Data Visualization: Plotly (plotly.express and plotly.graph_objects) for multi-axis climate timelines, pressure gauges, and scenario comparison charts
  • Data Sources & APIs: NASA POWER Temporal Monthly Point API (community="AG") via Python requests, paired with a structured JSON crop attribute knowledge base (rotation_knowledge_base.json)

Creativity & Factors Considered

Rather than building an opaque "black-box" recommendation engine that tells farmers what to plant without explanation, FieldShift treats the farm as a living system with a measurable history (Earth Memory) and an ecological balance sheet (Soil Debt). The addition of the Why Not? transparency framework directly addresses real-world adoption barriers in agriculture by openly stating model uncertainties and reminding growers to verify local planting calendars, soil pH/salinity, pest history, water rights, and market demand before acting. The architecture is also modularly designed for next-stage integration with NASA SMAP soil moisture, Landsat/MODIS NDVI time series, and SoilGrids data.

Our Vision: Every field has a memory. Every decision shapes its future.
